chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fadhl from Ali ibn al-Hasan al-Jarmi from Muhammad ibn Ziyad ibn Isa from Aban ibn Uthman from Abu Basir from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him):

That a man died during the time of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), and he used to sell dates, so his brother took the dates, and he had daughters. So his wife came to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and informed him of that. So Allah revealed to him, and the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) took the dates from the uncle and gave them to the daughters.

key_terms.الْعَمِّ: The uncle (paternal brother of the deceased)
key_terms.عَهْدِ النَّبِيِّ: During the time of the Prophet

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a deceased man's estate when he leaves behind daughters and a brother who takes possession of the goods?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* illustrates the early application of inheritance principles where the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) directly allocated the deceased's assets to his daughters, bypassing the brother who had taken possession. It highlights the distinct Shia and Sunni understanding of the 'uncle' (brother of the deceased) as a potential heir or possessor in the absence of other close relatives, while affirming the daughters' primary claim to the estate. The narrative serves as a practical precedent for the distribution of movable wealth before the codification of the detailed shares in Surah An-Nisa.
